idiom_name: record header object + Map of parser functions
implementation_notes: The property channel comes from the client library (kafkajs puts a headers object on every produced message, amqplib puts options.headers on publish), and the registry collapses into an ordinary Map or object from token to parse function - the local idiom that replaces the classic registry class. JSON.parse cannot help here: it only sees the text, so its reviver runs after parsing and can at most inspect fields already inside the payload, which is the content-based sibling. Read the header first, then hand the payload to the selected parser exactly once.
pitfalls: A header key can appear more than once, and kafkajs hands you an array for that case; comparing the array to a string silently fails, so normalise it once at the boundary.
JSON.parse's reviver never sees the headers, so type-driven revival is impossible - any classification inside a reviver is content-based parsing under another name.
Plain-object registries inherit from Object.prototype (readers['constructor'] is truthy); use a Map or Object.create(null).
